retention.stated: a database is archived after 10 days of inactivity on a free plan, and an archived database must be unarchived before it can be used; a deleted database has no point-in-time restore on Free and the Free column shows 1-day audit logs

egress.terms: no egress charge and no transfer allowance is published; the metered quantities are rows read and rows written, so a byte of egress is not what is counted

record.chaining: a free SQLite replica per tenant suits multi-tenant read-heavy work that a single free Postgres cannot hold, provided something touches each database at least every 10 days, because the free plan archives an inactive one

record.reliability_note: an inactive database on a free plan is archived after 10 days and must be unarchived before use; the archive is not a deletion and the data survives it

evidence.proved: Free column: 100 databases, 5GB storage, 500 Million rows read, 10 Million rows written, 3GB sync, 1 day audit logs; Developer USD 4.99 gives unlimited databases and 9GB
'Databases get archived after 10 days of inactivity for users on a free plan'; the unarchive command restores one
the platform API exposes a group unarchive endpoint, so the archive state is reachable programmatically and not only through the CLI
an unauthenticated GET returns 401 with 'token contains an invalid number of segments', proving the platform API exists and is token-authenticated

record.notes: The 500-database and 9-GB figures in circulation are the Developer plan, not Free. The 5 GB is a total, so 100 databases average 50 MB each. The binding constraint is not either number: it is the 10-day archive, which a quarterly job meets first and which nothing on the pricing page states.
record.binding_note: 10 days of inactivity archives the database on the free plan, so a job that runs less often than that finds the database unavailable. The 5 GB total and the 10-million-row monthly write budget are larger than that clock allows a quarterly job to reach.

history.title: Turso's free plan was recorded as having no idle clock, and it archives an inactive database after 10 days

card.summary: 5 GB total storage, 100 databases on Free

free_tier.stated: 5 GB total storage, 100 databases on Free

egress.terms: Not separately metered on Free; the binding meters are 500M rows read / 10M rows written per month, plus 3 GB embedded syncs. Serving files out of SQLite blobs burns rows-read, not bytes.

record.tooling: Turso CLI + HTTP API (`/v2/pipeline`), libSQL clients (JS/Python/Rust/Go), `turso db shell`, embedded replicas
record.chaining: 100 databases is a unit multiplier for ORGANIZATION, but the 5 GB storage is an ACCOUNT-level pot, not per database. 100 DBs x 50 MB each rather than 100 x 5 GB. Second axis: each org/account. Multiply accounts (GitHub OAuth is one click). N accounts x 5 GB.
record.limits_note: 5 GB is a hard total across all 100 DBs. This is the key trap: the big number is database COUNT, not storage. Exceeding rows-read returns `BLOCKED`. 3 GB sync cap for embedded replicas.
record.reliability_note: Exceeding quota returns BLOCKED errors on queries rather than data loss; DBs stay warm (no cold starts since Mar 2025).
